messages:
priya: Hey team — AcmeHealth flagged a Dedicated reservation ask. They want an 8-GPU baseline (A100-equivalent) for steady throughput (~50 reqs/s, avg seq 1024) with the ability to burst up to 24 GPUs for ~1 hour windows. They also want a 99.9% SLA and canary rollout. What do we need to scope and what are the tradeoffs?

jordan: Thanks Priya. Can you confirm p95 latency SLO (end-to-end) and whether they can accept quantized models or require fp16/float32? Also any compliance needs?

priya: p95 target is <300ms per token end-to-end. They said they prefer fp16 initially (no quant) but will consider quantization if it keeps accuracy within 2-3%. Compliance: SOC2 ok, no special needs.

alex: 24 A100s burst is a big ask. We size by tokens/sec and batching. Quick question: is the 50 reqs/s steady for sustained daily or just peak windows? That changes pool sizing. I'll run a throughput sim given model family.

marta: Ops note — our Dedicated pools support autoscale with a burst_capacity knob + prewarm. We also need pre-provision lead time for reserved nodes (hardware allocation). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-sizing (internal).

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Created ticket RED-3421 for Dedicated provisioning request: https://redwood.internal/tickets/RED-3421

alex: Preliminary config sketch:
```
pool:
  min_gpus: 8
  max_gpus: 24
  burst_capacity: 16
  prewarm: true
  cooldown: 10m
  autoscale_policy: target_tokens_per_gpu: 2000
```
If they adopt int8/quant, effective capacity ~2.5x so we can reduce baseline. Also, network egress impact during burst needs checking.

jordan: For launch criteria we need: (1) perf tests at 75% of claimed steady load showing p95 < target, (2) canary with 10% traffic and rollback plan, (3) cost estimate + customer consent on burst billing, (4) runbook and run-through with oncall. Also document fallback to a smaller model variant if latency regresses.

priya: I'll ask AcmeHealth to confirm traffic shape (sustained vs short bursts) and whether they'll accept quantization tradeoffs. Also asked about SLA credits — finance wants to precompute if we can support 99.9%.

marta: Ops actionables: we need a provisioning window (lead time), updated autoscale policy template, and prewarm automation for scheduled bursts. I'll start a draft policy and slot it for review.

alex: Action items for engineering: I'll run microbenchmarks + sim tomorrow and post numbers (GPU tokens/sec, expected batch sizes, cost/hr estimate). If model stays fp16 we need more GPUs than if they quantize.

jordan: I'll draft a customer-facing rollout + SLA doc and include rollback & canary steps, plus the success metrics for go/no-go.

priya: Summary of next steps: (1) Alex: throughput sims + cost by EOD tomorrow; (2) Jordan: SLA/rollout draft; (3) Marta: ops policy draft and provisioning lead time; (4) Priya: confirm quantization and traffic window with AcmeHealth.
